cases.sentence: Долохов же, прежде, в Москве, носивший персидский костюм, теперь, напротив, имел вид самого чопорного ___.
cases.explain: «гвардейского офицера» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Denísov wore a Cossack coat, had a beard, had an icon of Nikoláy the Wonder-Worker on his breast, and his way of speaking and everything he did indicated his unusual position. But Dólokhov, who in Moscow had worn a Persian costume, had now the appearance of a most correct officer of the Guards. He was clean-shaven and wore a Guardsman’s padded coat with an Order of St. George at his buttonhole and a plain forage cap set straight on his head. He took off his wet felt cloak in a corner of the room, and without greeting anyone went up to Denísov and began questioning him about the matter in hand. Denísov told him of the designs the large detachments had on the transport, of the message Pétya had brought, and his own replies to both generals. Then he told him all he knew of the French detachment.

cases.sentence: — рассеянно отвечал Долохов, вглядываясь в лицо ___.
cases.explain: «французского барабанщика» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Why not?” Dólokhov answered absently, scrutinizing the face of the French drummer boy. “Have you had that youngster with you long?” he asked Denísov.

cases.translation: The esaul, screwing up his light-colored eyes, nodded approvingly.
